pairs.locus: Bernard of Cluny, De Contemptu Mundi 2.127-128
pairs.question: Unde quid ordiar? Unde subaudiar? Eloquar unde?
pairs.answer: Unde Deus monet, ipse quod os sonet afflat abunde.
pairs.derivation: Author asks whence he should begin/be heard/speak; the next line answers 'whence God prompts...'. Question is the contiguous triple-question line; answer is the single following line (ends at its full stop). Nothing cut.

pairs.locus: Bernard of Cluny, De Contemptu Mundi 2.129-130
pairs.question: Quid prius insequar? An mala persequar, an bona strata?
pairs.answer: Stant mala, ius latet, hinc satirae patet area lata.
pairs.derivation: Author asks what to pursue first, evils or fallen goods; answers that evils stand and justice hides, hence the broad field of satire lies open. Answer is the single following line to its full stop; nothing cut.

pairs.locus: Bernard of Cluny, De Contemptu Mundi 2.329-330
pairs.question: In vitium tener est homo degener, altus et imus. Cur?
pairs.answer: Quia corpore non animo fore vult quasi primus.
pairs.derivation: Setup line included so 'Cur?' has a referent (the degenerate man inclined to vice). Question normalized to terminal '?'; answer is the 'Quia...' clause to its full stop. Nothing cut.

pairs.locus: Bernard of Cluny, De Contemptu Mundi 2.521-522
pairs.question: O mala tempora! Cur?
pairs.answer: Quia stercora tot pepererunt, tantaque sordida, ne loquar horrida, tanta dederunt.
pairs.derivation: Apostrophe 'O mala tempora!' included as referent for 'Cur?'. Answer is the 'quia...' explanation running to the full stop after 'dederunt'; first word capitalized. Nothing cut interior.

pairs.locus: Bernard of Cluny, De Contemptu Mundi 2.783-784
pairs.question: O mala secula! Cur?
pairs.derivation: Apostrophe included as referent for 'Cur?'. The 'quia...' clause is a complete because-answer ending at the semicolon; stopped there rather than continuing to the unrelated next line 'Promptus ad extima...'. Terminal semicolon normalized to full stop; first word capitalized.

pairs.locus: Bernard of Cluny, De Contemptu Mundi 2.811-812
pairs.question: Flaccus Horatius, et Cato, Persius et Iuvenalis: quid facerent si foret his modo vita sodalis?
pairs.answer: Temporis istius acta Lucilius ille stuperet, et sua prospera sanctaque tempora non reticeret.
pairs.derivation: Setup naming the satirists (line 810) kept so 'facerent' has a subject. Framing 'rogo' ('I ask') dropped as speech-act narration per the prompt. Answer is the first full sentence of the reply (to the full stop after 'reticeret'), saying Lucilius would be astounded and not keep silent; later elaborating lines ('Diceret optima...') omitted.

pairs.locus: Bernard of Cluny, De Contemptu Mundi 2.931-932
pairs.question: O mala secula! Cur?
pairs.answer: Quia singula nunc vitiantur, illaque luxibus, improbitatibus ista ligantur.
pairs.derivation: Apostrophe included as referent for 'Cur?'. Answer is the 'quia...' explanation to the full stop after 'ligantur'; first word capitalized. Nothing cut interior.
